dependencies: Each dot requires both matching inputs; each accumulator update depends on the preceding k update; store requires the final reduction. Next-k input fetches could be independent of current dot work if storage and runtime support permit it.
Different output tiles are independent assuming disjoint output addresses and no input/output aliasing that changes later reads. Those interface guarantees are not supplied.
edge_cases: Pinned dimensions are divisible by 16 and do not exercise masks. Test sub-tile and nonmultiple M/N/K dimensions, K tails, and output guard regions.
Require positive tile size and establish zero-size and K=0 behavior. Preserve float32 semantics; dot ordering, rounding, special values and acceptable tolerances are not fully specified.
layout_memory: The logical float32 accumulator is tile by tile: 1024 bytes at tile=16 if fully materialized. Strides, physical layout, alignment, memory spaces, bank mapping and compiler allocation are unspecified.
Masked loads do not specify masked-off fill values. K-tail elements must contribute zero. Extra accumulators or pipeline buffers need checked storage capacity and lifetimes.
loops: Loop order is i over M, j over N, k over K, stepping by tile. The supplied shape has two i positions, two j positions and four k positions per output tile: four output tiles and sixteen source-level dot calls. These are static counts, not execution measurements.
An A(i,k) tile is requested again for each j; a B(k,j) tile again for each i. Multiple live output accumulators can expose reuse across one outer dimension.
movement: Each k iteration requests two masked input tiles; each output tile is stored once. Assuming full 16x16 float32 materialization, no cache reuse and no spills, 32 input-tile loads plus four output-tile stores at 1024 bytes each give 36864 logical bytes. This is a source traffic model, not measured memory or DMA traffic.
Actual traffic depends on lowering, transactions, cache reuse, staging and spills. Event counts alone cannot identify exposed transfer time.
stages: The complete pinned source is a synthetic, explicitly never-executed matmul fixture. Each output tile initializes a float32 zero accumulator, repeatedly loads left and right tiles, performs dot and accumulation, then stores a masked output tile. The contract is C = A @ B, not accumulation into an existing C.

A's declared configuration is tile=16 and dtype=float32 for M=32, N=32, K=64. Source/config/build digests and run bindings describe the intended recipe; they do not prove that a runtime loaded this code.
synchronization: No explicit asynchronous operations, waits or barriers appear. Source order encodes dependencies, not whether the compiler overlaps operations.
An explicit pipeline must wait for both active inputs before dot and prevent buffer reuse before its last reader finishes; output store follows the complete reduction.

dependencies: Each dot requires both inputs; the accumulator serializes its k reduction; store consumes the final result. Packed input readiness must precede consumption.

The finer tiling requests each left tile across four j positions and each right tile across four i positions. Grouped outputs can reduce repeated requests while increasing live accumulator state.

plans.mechanism: Reuse each left tile across grouped output-column tiles
plans.modification: From A-parent, retain tile=16 and float32. Group two adjacent j tiles, initialize one accumulator per valid member, then for each k load left(a,i,k) once and load/update each member's right(b,k,j) and accumulator. Store valid outputs after reduction, preserving each output's k order and masks.
risks: Extra live accumulators can spill or create resource pressure.
Group tails can read/store out of bounds.
Reuse assumes valid input/output independence and aliasing rules.
tradeoffs: Fewer explicit left loads require more live accumulator state and scheduling complexity.
Caches/lowering may already provide reuse, so physical traffic may not fall.
unknowns: Lowering, layout, cache reuse and resource limits.
Whether repeated left loads are exposed on the dependency path.
Numerical tolerance and aliasing guarantees.

correctness: Compare with a trusted float32 C=A@B reference on the pinned shape, sub-tile/nonmultiple M/N/K, odd group tails and supported K=0; inspect output guard regions.
Preserve each output's k order, accumulation dtype and masks; establish any missing tolerance/aliasing contract.
performance: Build identified parent and grouping-only variants with fixed tile/dtype/layout; verify loaded source/config/build and candidate/run/context binding.
Use repeated matched measurements with warmup and synchronized end-to-end timing; report distributions.
Collect candidate-bound bytes, cache effects, spills/resources and dependency traces to test whether fewer loads reduce exposed time. Lower latency alone does not prove bandwidth improvement.

variants: Group size one as the control and two as the primary reuse variant.
Separately test a bounded larger group on larger-N shapes, preserving tile/dtype and recording resource use.

plans.mechanism: Overlap next-k transfers with current-k dot computation
plans.modification: Separately from A-parent at tile=16/float32, introduce two alternating left/right input-buffer pairs. Prime the first k pair, schedule the next valid pair into inactive buffers while computing the current pair, wait for readiness before dot and last use before overwrite, then drain and store. Preserve one accumulator, original k ordering and masks; never prefetch past valid K.
risks: Read-before-ready or overwrite-before-consume races can corrupt output.
Asynchronous progress may be unsupported or contend with compute.
Extra storage, waits and startup/drain may cause spills or regression.
tradeoffs: Hides potential transfer latency without eliminating bytes, at added memory and synchronization cost.
Four k tiles leave limited steady-state depth; ideal models omit overhead and contention.
unknowns: Asynchronous APIs, engine independence and synchronization semantics.
Actual stage times, waits and capacity.
Whether original lowering already overlaps operations or another stage dominates.

correctness: Compare parent/reference across one, two and many K tiles, partial K/M/N tails and supported zero-size cases.
Stress repeated launches and changing inputs to detect stale-buffer races; verify readiness, last-use and masked zero fill.
Hold dtype and accumulation order fixed under documented tolerances.
performance: Capture an identity-bound dependency trace showing readiness, consumption, waits and reuse before claiming exposed transfer latency; counts alone are insufficient.
Measure parent and serial/double-storage/overlap ablations under matched hardware, shape and dtype; include allocation, startup, drain and synchronization.
Report measured exposed-time/resource changes. The separate 14 s hypothetical prediction is not a hardware speedup; a real target run is required for a performance claim.

variants: Serial parent, serial schedule with doubled storage, and asynchronous one-tile lookahead to isolate allocation versus overlap.
A separately identified prefetch-only variant if explicit asynchronous tiles are unsupported, with no promise of overlap.

plans.modification: From B-parent with tile=8/float32 fixed, prepare a precisely indexed tile-major B representation and replace right=load(b,k,j,tile) with its packed-block read. Preserve mathematical K-by-N indexing and masks. Initially pack once per invocation before compute so preparation is included; do not assume an unestablished immutable/reusable B contract.

Duplicating compiler conversion or worsening locality.
Scratch and conversion overhead exceeding gains on the small workload.

correctness: Use asymmetric known matrices to expose accidental transpose, then random/cancellation-sensitive cases with established float32 tolerances.

Group two adjacent j tiles, initialize one accumulator per valid member, then for each k load left(a,i,k) once and load/update each member's right(b,k,j) and accumulator. Store valid outputs after reduction, preserving each output's k order and masks.
risks: Extra live accumulators can spill or create resource pressure.
Group tails can read/store out of bounds.
Reuse assumes valid input/output independence and aliasing rules.
tradeoffs: Fewer explicit left loads require more live accumulator state and scheduling complexity.
Caches/lowering may already provide reuse, so physical traffic may not fall.
unknowns: Lowering, layout, cache reuse and resource limits.
Whether repeated left loads are exposed on the dependency path.
Numerical tolerance and aliasing guarantees.

correctness: Compare with a trusted float32 C=A@B reference on the pinned shape, sub-tile/nonmultiple M/N/K, odd group tails and supported K=0; inspect output guard regions.

Use repeated matched measurements with warmup and synchronized end-to-end timing; report distributions.

variants: Group size one as the control and two as the primary reuse variant.
Separately test a bounded larger group on larger-N shapes, preserving tile/dtype and recording resource use.

plans.mechanism: Overlap next-k transfers with current-k dot computation
plans.modification: Separately from A-parent at tile=16/float32, introduce two alternating left/right input-buffer pairs. Prime the first k pair, schedule the next valid pair into inactive buffers while computing the current pair, wait for readiness before dot and last use before overwrite, then drain and store. Preserve one accumulator, original k ordering and masks; never prefetch past valid K.
risks: Read-before-ready or overwrite-before-consume races can corrupt output.
Asynchronous progress may be unsupported or contend with compute.
Extra storage, waits and startup/drain may cause spills or regression.
tradeoffs: Hides potential transfer latency without eliminating bytes, at added memory and synchronization cost.
Four k tiles leave limited steady-state depth; ideal models omit overhead and contention.
unknowns: Asynchronous APIs, engine independence and synchronization semantics.
Actual stage times, waits and capacity.
Whether original lowering already overlaps operations or another stage dominates.

correctness: Compare parent/reference across one, two and many K tiles, partial K/M/N tails and supported zero-size cases.
Stress repeated launches and changing inputs to detect stale-buffer races; verify readiness, last-use and masked zero fill.
Hold dtype and accumulation order fixed under documented tolerances.

Report measured exposed-time/resource changes. The separate 14 s hypothetical prediction is not a hardware speedup; a real target run is required for a performance claim.

variants: Serial parent, serial schedule with doubled storage, and asynchronous one-tile lookahead to isolate allocation versus overlap.
A separately identified prefetch-only variant if explicit asynchronous tiles are unsupported, with no promise of overlap.

plans.mechanism: Explicit right-operand layout preparation reusable across dot calls
plans.modification: From B-parent with tile=8/float32 fixed, prepare a precisely indexed tile-major B representation and replace right=load(b,k,j,tile) with its packed-block read. Preserve mathematical K-by-N indexing and masks. Initially pack once per invocation before compute so preparation is included; do not assume an unestablished immutable/reusable B contract.
risks: Packed-index mistakes or unintended mathematical transpose.
Duplicating compiler conversion or worsening locality.
Scratch and conversion overhead exceeding gains on the small workload.
tradeoffs: Potentially better block access/less repeated conversion requires extra storage and preparation traffic.
Compute-only improvement can accompany end-to-end regression; report both boundaries explicitly.
unknowns: Original strides, alignment, dot layout and implicit conversions.
B ownership/lifetime and repeated-use guarantees.
Packing cost, capacity and whether layout work is critical.

correctness: Use asymmetric known matrices to expose accidental transpose, then random/cancellation-sensitive cases with established float32 tolerances.

plans.mechanism: Reuse right tiles across output-row accumulators
plans.modification: Separately from B-parent at tile=8/float32, group two i output tiles per j and maintain a separate accumulator for each valid member. In original k order, load right(b,k,j) once, load each left(a,i,k), update that member, and store outputs after reduction. Preserve both group-tail and element-tail masks.
risks: Additional accumulators spill or reduce execution capacity.
Loop changes mishandle i tails or output addresses.
Fewer source requests fail to reduce external-memory traffic.
tradeoffs: Fewer right-tile requests require more live output state and scheduling complexity.
Small groups bound resources but capture only part of possible reuse; larger groups increase pressure.
unknowns: Existing cache reuse, load cost and exposed dependency time.
Compiler allocation and safe target-specific group sizes.
Tolerance, aliasing contract and representative shapes.

dependencies: Each dot requires both matching inputs; each accumulator update depends on the preceding k update; store requires the final reduction. Next-k input fetches could be independent of current dot work if storage and runtime support permit it.
Different output tiles are independent assuming disjoint output addresses and no input/output aliasing that changes later reads. Those interface guarantees are not supplied.
edge_cases: Pinned dimensions are divisible by 16 and do not exercise masks. Test sub-tile and nonmultiple M/N/K dimensions, K tails, and output guard regions.
Require positive tile size and establish zero-size and K=0 behavior. Preserve float32 semantics; dot ordering, rounding, special values and acceptable tolerances are not fully specified.
layout_memory: The logical float32 accumulator is tile by tile: 1024 bytes at tile=16 if fully materialized. Strides, physical layout, alignment, memory spaces, bank mapping and compiler allocation are unspecified.
Masked loads do not specify masked-off fill values. K-tail elements must contribute zero. Extra accumulators or pipeline buffers need checked storage capacity and lifetimes.
loops: Loop order is i over M, j over N, k over K, stepping by tile. The supplied shape has two i positions, two j positions and four k positions per output tile: four output tiles and sixteen source-level dot calls. These are static counts, not execution measurements.
An A(i,k) tile is requested again for each j; a B(k,j) tile again for each i. Multiple live output accumulators can expose reuse across one outer dimension.
movement: Each k iteration requests two masked input tiles; each output tile is stored once. Assuming full 16x16 float32 materialization, no cache reuse and no spills, 32 input-tile loads plus four output-tile stores at 1024 bytes each give 36864 logical bytes. This is a source traffic model, not measured memory or DMA traffic.
Actual traffic depends on lowering, transactions, cache reuse, staging and spills. Event counts alone cannot identify exposed transfer time.
stages: The complete pinned source is a synthetic, explicitly never-executed matmul fixture. Each output tile initializes a float32 zero accumulator, repeatedly loads left and right tiles, performs dot and accumulation, then stores a masked output tile. The contract is C = A @ B, not accumulation into an existing C.

A's declared configuration is tile=16 and dtype=float32 for M=32, N=32, K=64. Source/config/build digests and run bindings describe the intended recipe; they do not prove that a runtime loaded this code.
synchronization: No explicit asynchronous operations, waits or barriers appear. Source order encodes dependencies, not whether the compiler overlaps operations.
An explicit pipeline must wait for both active inputs before dot and prevent buffer reuse before its last reader finishes; output store follows the complete reduction.

dependencies: Each dot requires both inputs; the accumulator serializes its k reduction; store consumes the final result. Packed input readiness must precede consumption.
Sharing a right tile across i outputs requires separate accumulators and correct masks. Preserve each output's k order to avoid an additional reduction-order change.
edge_cases: The pinned shape is divisible by 8. Test smaller/nonmultiple dimensions, odd output groups, partial K panels and output bounds.
Packing must preserve C[i,j] = sum_k A[i,k]*B[k,j]; a physical transpose must not transpose the mathematical operand. Establish zero-size, aliasing, special-value and tolerance rules.
layout_memory: One logical 8x8 float32 accumulator occupies 256 bytes if materialized. Strides, alignment, layout transformations, cache behavior, resource allocation and spill thresholds are unavailable.
More accumulators extend live state; packed B needs additional storage with explicit ownership and lifetime. Capacity and sustainable bandwidth are unknown.
loops: The i,j,k loops use a uniform tile. At M=N=32 and K=64, tile=8 gives four i positions, four j positions and eight k positions: sixteen output tiles and 128 source-level dot calls. These are source-derived predictions, not compiler or hardware counts.
The finer tiling requests each left tile across four j positions and each right tile across four i positions. Grouped outputs can reduce repeated requests while increasing live accumulator state.
movement: There are 256 source input-tile loads and sixteen output-tile stores. Assuming full 8x8 float32 tiles, no cache reuse and no spills, each is 256 bytes and the logical total is 69632 bytes. This cannot establish actual device traffic or explain the synthetic benchmark.
Packing B could change access and conversion costs, but the current source does not show whether B is strided, already packed or directly dot-compatible. Packing adds reads, writes and allocation.
stages: B's complete pinned synthetic source initializes a float32 accumulator per output tile, repeatedly loads left/right tiles and accumulates dot products, then performs a masked store for C = A @ B.

Its declared tile=8, dtype=float32 recipe and B-run binding are distinct from A. The matching loop structure cannot make A's profile B's evidence, and the recipe does not prove a real loaded executable.
synchronization: No explicit synchronization or pipeline appears. Serial source calls do not prove a measured serialized critical path.
A shared tile remains live until all grouped dots finish. Concurrent packing would require producer/consumer readiness and no overwrite before the final use.

alternatives: Cache/compiler reuse already captures the opportunity.
Extra accumulators spill or reduce useful concurrency.
Compute or fixed invocation overhead dominates.

hypotheses.text: If B's physical layout causes repeated strided reads or implicit conversions, explicit tile-major packing may reduce exposed access/conversion cost.

alternatives: Existing cache reuse makes extra live state unnecessary.
More accumulators cause spills or worse scheduling.
Tile-8 dot/dispatch overhead dominates, so load reuse alone is insufficient.

observations.text: A's complete history contains four dependency records and ten owned records: task/workload/context/baseline, Route A, original Plan, A-candidate from baseline, A-run, running/succeeded events, timing/benchmark and trace/profile. It gives one original candidate/run, not isolated optimization trials. New Plans must use requested A-parent wrapping A-candidate, not historical baseline. The predicate checks the completeness flag only; it cannot verify causality or loaded-code identity.

B's complete history contains task/workload/context/baseline plus Route B, original Plan, B-candidate from baseline, B-run, running/succeeded events, timing/benchmark and trace/profile. It provides one original candidate/run with no controlled predecessor comparison. Requested B-parent wraps B-candidate; baseline is ancestry, not the new Plan parent. History completeness is not proof of a real loaded executable.

The packet reports A-run/A-candidate in context as a confirmed, valid synthetic 10 ms timing with correctness passed. This is a fixture evidence fact, not a new CPU/TPU measurement or a causal explanation. Sample distributions and tolerance coverage are absent.

The packet reports B-run/B-candidate in context as a confirmed, valid synthetic 12 ms timing with correctness passed. This B-bound fact does not explain a mechanism or authorize cancellation. Separate scenario microsecond values cannot replace these benchmark milliseconds.

A-profile is available and bound to A-run, but exposed A-trace content only names target matmul. Dependency intervals, waits, bytes, compiler resources and hardware rates are absent; artifact digests are not those missing contents. Separately, 1000 DMA events with null bytes/waits/critical path and 50 us execution do not identify a bottleneck. The missing-wait scenario explicitly lacks parser support: unavailable wait is unknown, not zero.

B-profile correctly references B-run/B-trace, but the exposed trace only names matmul. No critical path, layout cost, bytes or resource limit is available. In the separate mismatch scenario, A-current/A owns the profile while B-current/B is requested. Matching workload cannot transfer measured identity. Recollect or rebind through verified B candidate, run and context.

At tile 16, A requests each left tile for two j outputs. Grouping those outputs with separate accumulators can request that left tile once while preserving right requests and each output's k reduction. This predicts fewer source requests, not necessarily fewer external-memory transactions or lower latency, since caching/lowering may already capture reuse.

B's tile-8 source repeats right-tile requests for different i outputs and hides physical layout behind load/dot. It supports two distinct investigation routes: retain a right tile across grouped outputs, or explicitly prepare a dot-compatible packed operand. Neither source structure nor synthetic latency establishes a limiting mechanism.

It lists synthetic CPU, has no local experiment references, and explicitly requires applicability/performance experiments. Source-supported is not locally validated.

Preserve its exact pinned excerpt/revision as stale evidence, mark the full original unavailable, and treat live-source refresh as new input. Do not silently replace revisions or assert current/local validation. The manifest separately declares no atomic combined snapshot and no consistent whole knowledge snapshot; one matching source cannot repair that limitation.

The scenario's buffering failure was on synthetic-H1, float32, 32x32. Current conditions are synthetic-H2, bfloat16, 4096x4096 without a retest. The old outcome remains historical; either current outcome is untested. It cannot cancel a legal current experiment. These scenario conditions do not replace B's pinned float32 tile-8 workload.

The tile/dtype scenario reports 20 to 12 us while both tile and dtype change, with no isolated variants or tolerance test: tile-only attribution is unresolved. Float32 to bfloat16 changes numerical semantics, traffic and instruction choices. The other scenario confirms 20 to 16 us in the same context after several scheduling/layout changes but has no profile. Faster timing is observed; bandwidth improvement is only a possible explanation alongside overlap, instruction count, cache/layout or synchronization. Controlled ablations and correctness tests are needed.

For the separate hypothetical model, assume four 3 s transfers, each feeding 2 s compute; independent transfer and compute resources overlap perfectly with sufficient buffers, no contention, no extra overhead and preserved dependencies. Ideal duration = 3 + 2 + (4-1)*max(3,2) = 14 s. This is a mathematical prediction with no real hardware run, not a TPU measurement or costs for A's 10 ms fixture.

On device 0/clock c0 only, [0,10], [2,5] and [8,12] have union [0,12], or 12 us. Adding durations to 17 us double counts coverage. Device 1/clock c1 is a separate clock domain and excluded. This synthetic trace-derived union is neither critical-path causality nor a real TPU measurement.

Policy retains both routes with at least two materially different Plans per exact parent. The scenario's 10 versus 12 us cannot cancel B or select a winner. The PlanSet retains A-parent and B-parent and does not change best.
